newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation 1.17 pct in May 16-June 15.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation 1.17 pct in May 16-June 15.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) edged up to 1.17 percent in the May 16-June 15 period versus 0.82 percent in the prior four-week period, a Fipe official said.

Fipe chief Juarez Rizzieri said a hike in bus fares combined with rising clothing prices and higher phone and electricity rates to drive up the Fipe index, which measures inflation in the Sao Paulo area.
He forecast inflation for June would reach slightly more than one percent due mostly to increases in telephone rates, bus fares and rises in some food prices.
Rizzieri released the following breakdown of Fipe's weighted inflation index for May 16 through June 15:
- Food: 0.17 pct rise in the month
- Housing: 2.37 pct rise in the month
- Transportation: 0.87 pct rise in the month
- Clothing: 4.20 pct rise in the month
- Health care: 1.01 pct rise in the month
- Education: 0.03 pct rise in the month
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
